gaps.what: Record that possession of the whole of North Island was taken under the order (who took it and on what date), or failing that, record that the $5,000,000 award was paid into court and a final order of condemnation entered or title vested. The Army was already on the island by permission before the order, and the 8 Sep 1917 Navy occupancy (secondary source) does not establish whole-island possession. The Cornell text of 255 U.S. 472, as extracted, contains no sentence on possession being taken, the President's order, or payment.

gaps.what: Whether any later instrument expressly revoked or superseded EO 2676-A. None is held or was found in the reviewed evidence; this is not a verified universal absence. The land remains Naval Air Station North Island, which is not itself evidence that the order still operates.
gaps.where_to_look: Later executive orders on North Island; EO 7215 (1935, interchange of property between War and Navy Departments) is an unread candidate that surfaced in search and was not checked for whether it names this order

moves.note: Held ProQuest replica of the State Department copy is legible in full; the order has one operative clause.

Operative status is OPEN with a named gap. The order is a one-time command to take possession of named property (rule e), but no source read establishes that possession of the whole island was taken under it. Navy occupancy on 8 Sep 1917 (NPS), the conditional condemnation judgment and its affirmance (255 U.S. 472) and the July 1919 purchase authorization (NPS) are leads toward performance, not proof of it.
The single clause is open: no record of execution of the whole-island possession command, and no record of payment of the award or entry of a final order of condemnation, was read.

review.conclusion_reason: Rule (e) requires evidence of performance. Navy occupancy of part of the island does not establish possession of the whole island under this order by September 8, 1917; conditional condemnation and purchase authorization do not independently establish completion. The result itself acknowledges this missing fact. Operative status should be OPEN pending a record establishing execution of the whole-island possession command, such as the condemnation record or War/Navy reports. Formal status can only remain 'no express ending found in reviewed evidence,' not a verified universal absence.
missed_evidence: Cornell opinion, https://www.law.cornell.edu/supremecourt/text/255/472, lines 70–72, addresses the government's contention that it took only upland, discusses the statutory and pleaded whole-island scope, and concludes 'Decree and judgment affirmed'. This strengthens the whole-island condemnation evidence but does not supply the execution date or establish payment of the conditional award.
review.stop_code_verdict: confirmed: WEB fits the first gap; the slice holds only the order and identifies no held performance record or later instrument resolving it. The cited public pages do not close that gap.
review.suspected_defect: The conclusion converts Navy occupancy on September 8, 1917 into a firm upper bound for completion of the whole-island command despite expressly retaining a gap about that performance. This is an unsupported inference rather than a fabricated quotation.
